(1) the fill of the nested dis-section algorithm can be reduced at the expense of parallelism, (2) the fill of nested dissection can be further reduced by a simple algorithm, and (3) nested dissection is not asymptotically optimal for the fill of Gaussian elimination on certain classes of graphs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the tradeoffs that exist between the amount of fill and the degree of parallelism that are possible for Gaussian elimination.
the tradeoff between parallelism and the number of fill-in operations required to perform Gaussian elimination.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, for the class of sparse matrices that we consider, LPND generates orders that are as parallel as those produced by standard nested dissection and significantly less fill than the orders generated by METIS, AMD, or BEND.

, in the context of Gaussian elimination on sparse symmetric matrices, LPND produces elimination orders that are as parallel as those produced by standard nested dissection and are less fill than those produced by METIS, AMD, and BEND, at the expense of a small reduction of parallelism.
